item.title: How Mick Cronin hyped up Bruins before bounce-back win vs. Georgetown
item.description: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images How Mick Cronin hyped up Bruins before bounce-back win vs. Georgetown appeared first on ClutchPoints . The UCLA Bruins suffered a disappointing defeat at the hands of the Saint Mary’s Gaels on Thursday afternoon, keeping them from advancing to the title game of the Rady Children’s Invitational. But the Bruins bounced back with a 75-63 win over Georgetown in the third-place game, and UCLA head coach Mick Cronin revealed how he challenged the team prior to the game, as per Connor David Dullinger of The LA Times. “I told the guys this is a chance to show what we’re made of. I challenged them pretty good last night,” Cronin said. “I told them that they need to have reverence and an appreciation for the jersey they wear … UCLA is a privilege to go there as a student.” With the win, UCLA improved to 7-1 on the season, although where they will fall when the new AP men’s basketball poll comes out on Monday, remains to be seen. The Bruins had been ranked at No. 6 coming into this past week. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was an unlikely hero who led the way for UCLA in sophomore guard Azavier Robinson, finishing with a game-high 23 points. Robinson is in his first season with the Bruins after entering the transfer portal following his freshman year at Butler. UCLA is in the program’s eighth season with Mick Cronin at the helm as head coach. During that time, he’s led the Bruins to five NCAA Tournament appearances, including one Final Four run in 2020-21. UCLA’s next game is Tuesday, Dec. 1 as they begin Big Ten play with a matchup against the Oregon Ducks. The seemingly innocuous comment reflected how much the tenor has changed since the 49ers beat Seattle 32-29 in Week 5. Before that game, 49ers players were asked about facing the defending Super Bowl champions who trampled them en route to a title last season. The Seahawks handed the 49ers their second-worst playoff loss in franchise history in a 41-6 divisional-round win after wresting the NFC's No. 1 seed from them with a 13-3 victory in the regular-season finale. All of the roster doesn't matter. The history doesn't matter. The only thing that matters is quarter one through four on Sunday." Healthy backfield: When the 49ers played the Seahawks on Oct. 11, they game-planned for the team's third-string running back. Emanuel Wilson had 20 carries for only 61 yards - and failed to break off a run longer than eight yards - in San Francisco's win. The Seahawks' offense looked one-dimensional. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the only true threat. Things will look much different this time around, as the 49ers will face Seattle's top two rushers in Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. Over their past three contests since returning a healthy Charbonnet and Price, the Seahawks' ground attack has vastly improved. Price, a rookie first-round pick, collected his first career touchdown in the Seahawks' last game before their bye week, a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Charbonnet, working his way back from a January torn ACL, has gone from six to 16 to 20 carries over his past three contests. He had a season-high 94 rushing yards against Las Vegas on Nov. 15. The 49ers lead the league in rushing yards allowed per game (81.2). Making Seattle's run game moot, in an expected rain game, could go a long way toward shutting down a passing offense that ranks in the bottom half of the league. With defensive tackles DeForest Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa and CJ West, plus defensive ends Bosa, Keion White and Mykel Williams all healthy, Sunday will provide a strong test as to how legitimate San Francisco's run defense truly is. Darnold returns: Quarterback Sam Darnold (quad) will return for Seattle after missing the team's past two games. The Seahawks said "thanks, but no thanks" to backup quarterback Drew Lock, who has led them to a 4-0 record across Darnold's two stretches of absences. Lock this season has a passer rating of 125.6. That would lead all quarterbacks who have started at least four games. Darnold's passer rating this season is 79.5. Head coach Mike Macdonald shut down speculation of Darnold losing his job while he was still out. On Nov. 16, asked about the possibility of inserting Lock for the remainder of the season, Macdonald said, "Drew's been fantastic. He's been phenomenal. … But Sam's our quarterback." The 49ers are 2-2 against Darnold as a Seahawk over the past 1½ seasons, including their 41-6 divisional round loss in January. Darnold's numbers over those four games: 667 passing yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions, 69.5% completion rate. Asked Friday if he feels the healthiest he's been all season, Darnold told local reporters: "I feel really good. I'm not going to compare it to any other point in the season, but I feel really good right now." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. Holiday-week scheduling always compresses the fantasy football calendar. Week 12 has already locked 10 teams out of managers’ lineup decisions. Between Wednesday’s Rams-Packers opener, Thursday’s Thanksgiving tripleheader, and Friday’s AFC tilt in Pittsburgh, nearly a third of the league’s wideouts are no longer available. This leaves managers scrambling to patch holes before Sunday’s slate kicks off. When a manager’s WR2 or flex spot takes a late hit, the sharpest pivot is isolating high-volume route trees, soft perimeter coverage, and pass-heavy game scripts. Still waiting to take the field, these four receivers bring genuine spike-week potential to save your Week 12 matchup . Carnell Tate , TEN (@ JAC) Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Carnell Tate travels south to EverBank Stadium to square off against AFC South rival Jacksonville. He returned from a multi-week absence in Week 11 against Dallas. Tate immediately announced his presence by hauling in two passes for 58 yards and a 59-yard touchdown while practicing in full throughout the week. Now, Tennessee enters Sunday as a heavy road underdog. Trailing game scripts virtually guarantee 35-plus pass attempts. They face a Jaguars defense that will allow garbage-time aerial production. That should funnel steady vertical targets and red-zone looks directly to Tate, giving him clear top-15 upside. That’s after erupting for nine receptions on 11 targets for 122 receiving yards in Washington’s thrilling 22-20 Monday night victory over Cincinnati in Week 11. Williams has established himself as a trusted vertical and intermediate weapon for quarterback Jayden Daniels. He now sits at 37 catches for 448 yards and two touchdowns across 10 games. item.title: ‘In a weird way’: Mason Rudolph shares how the Aaron Rodgers drama actually helped Steelers beat Broncos
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers capped off a very difficult week with a fine win over the Denver Broncos. The drama surrounding Aaron Rodgers, who was released earlier this week, dominated the headlines, and many felt that would have an impact on the team. However, the Steelers were incredibly dominant, beating the Broncos 27-5. Mason Rudolph says the Aaron Rodgers ‘adversity’ brought the Steelers together Mason Rudolph hadn’t been involved in first-team reps all week, which is why he had to put in extra work on Thursday ahead of Friday’s game. The quarterback, who took over Rodgers’ role, definitely played his part, delivering a clean, efficient and turnover-free game-manager performance. Unsurprisingly, the questions after the game were always going to be dominated by the Rodgers saga during the week. Rudolph was asked about it too, and he claimed that the controversy helped, as it brought the team a lot closer ahead of the win against the Broncos. He said on Prime Video: “It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented, nothing I’ve ever been through and probably the same for all my teammates. “We’re so proud of the way we turned the page on Wednesday, and the veteran leadership – Cameron Heyward, Jalen Ramsey, T. J. Watt – really led us forward.” Rudolph further added: “I think the leadership council just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy. And I think, in a weird way, you know, the adversity brought us probably closer together. And I think we’ll just keep carrying that into week after week.” The 31-year-old hadn’t started a game for over a year, so the pressure was on for him to deliver after taking Rodgers’ place against the Broncos. Rudolph finished the game with nine of 15 passes completed (60.0%) for 142 yards and one touchdown. He took a sack for a 12-yard loss, which was really the only blemish in his performance, while posting a 113.8 passer rating. All in all, it was a fine outing for the Steelers after what has been a tough week. We’re sure Rudolph and everyone else will be delighted with how the game panned out. item.title: NDSU Successfully Debuts New QB vs. SJSU
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 10: Preston Brown #0 of the North Dakota State Bison runs against Kal-El Togafau #44 of the UNLV Rebels at Allegiant Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Louis Grasse/Getty Images) Getty Injuries finally caught up with North Dakota State senior quarterback Nathan Hayes after 11 games this season. His oblique injury kept him out of Friday’s game against San Jose State, so the Bison debuted freshman quarterback Preston Brown in his first career start. Brown started with a bang on a 49-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Jackson Williams in the first quarter. The Missouri native kept it going in the first half, leading four scoring drives to a 24-7 lead, and he did enough to help the Bison hold on to a 38-31 win in San Jose. Brown went 12-23 for 226 yards and a touchdown versus an interception. He also rushed for 31 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. His rushing score came when the Bison needed it most in the fourth quarter to make it 38-24, which capped a six-play, 71-yard scoring drive. Brown also had ample support for the running game in his debut with 183 yards and three touchdowns overall. Bison Skill Players Step Up Running back D.J. Scott led the way with 86 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries. Fellow running back Nyeoti Punni rushed for 34 yards on five carries. Running back Barry Kpeenu also chipped in 16 yards on five carries, and he had a 21-yard reception. Wide receiver Chris Kiel had 12 yards on two carries, and he caught a 51-yard pass. Brown also connected well with Williams in the passing game, as the lead wideout had seven catches for 117 yards and the score. Wide receiver Jordan McCants had a 20-yard reception, and Brown spread the ball around to six different pass catchers overall. NDSU Waits Next NDSU improved to 10-2 overall and will await this weekend’s Mountain West Conference results to see if they land in the title game. Winning helped the Bison if things came down to a tiebreaker based on computer ratings amid a logjam of conference teams with 6-2 league records. The Mountain West championship game is Dec. 4, and the matchup will be known after the UNLV-Nevada game on Saturday. item.description: The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team's season ended with a state semifinal loss to Somers on Friday in Middletown. Ty Starr made sure the Spartans were not shut out when the senior took a handoff and swept off the left side for a 56-yard touchdown run with 18 seconds left in the game. item.title: UH plays like a No. 1 to beat Oakland behind Mercy Miller's career-high 23 points
item.description: Houston guard Mercy Miller, right, collides with Oakland forward Nate Ahner, left, during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, in Houston. (AP Photo/Kevin M. Cox) (Kevin M. Cox/Associated Press) Mercy Miller set a career-high with 23 points as No. 1 Houston cruised to a 77-46 win over Oakland at the Fertitta Center on Friday night. UH (7-0) was playing its first game since moving into the top spot after sweeping three games at the Players Era 8 tournament, including wins over then-No. 1 Florida and No. 11 Kansas. Miller set his previous career-high with 21 points in the all-Big 12 final against the Jayhawks. Chendall Weaver , who received a temporary injunction Wednesday that allows him to remain eligible for the rest of the season, added 14 points and five rebounds off the bench. The Cougars jumped out to a 21-2 lead, sparked by 3-pointers by Miller and Weavers, and held the Grizzlies to just two field goals in the first 8 1/2 minutes. Joseph Tugler finished with four points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block for the Cougars, who have won 44 consecutive regular-season games against unranked opponents. Miller scored 12 of UH's first 17 points to begin the second half, pushing the lead to 58-26. He finished 7-of-10 shooting and 6-of-6 from the free-throw line. Chris Fields Jr. scored 10 points for Oakland, a member of the Horizon League that was coming off a 46-point loss at Purdue. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. They’re two of the best players to ever wear black and gold and when they’re done playing, they have dates with gold jackets waiting. The Steelers defense scored 14 points off turnovers and allowed only three. “Yeah, after the last two games, we haven’t provided short fields,” Heyward said. “We haven’t provided splash enough, and I thought we did that today. I thought we took care of the run early, got a touchdown by T.J. and a touchdown by Jalen. Just giving them a little bit more short fields. When things are just a little bit gone awry, I think you’ve got to provide that for your oﬀense.” They also did it from the very beginning of the game. The crowd at Acrisure Stadium on Friday was reflective of the weird week the team had. There were “Go, Pack Go,” chants, mocking McCarthy’s blunder in Philly the week before, and also “F*** Aaron Rodgers” chants. But if things went sideways, if the Steelers started like they had the week before, the restlessness could have gotten awfully loud. “Huge,” Watt said. “I mean, keeping the crowd into it — the crowd was incredible tonight from the start. We most definitely feed oﬀ of them and they kept us going throughout the whole night.” Instead, it was Watt with a huge play to open the game, scoring a touchdown on a first-quarter fumble recover that put the Steelers ahead for good. It will face challenges down the way from an Xs and Os and talent-level standpoints. They don’t have a quarterback like a Joe Burrow, a Josh Allen or a Patrick Mahomes. But if the challenge is mental, a question of fortitude or toughness or the ability to bring people together in the pursuit of a common goal, then don’t count the Steelers out. They’ll prove you wrong. Trust me, I know. item.title: What's next for USWNT? USA women qualify for 2027 World Cup with win over El Salvador, gun for CONCACAF title
item.description: What's next for USWNT? USA women qualify for 2027 World Cup with win over El Salvador, gun for CONCACAF title originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The U.S. women smacked El Salvador 8-0, advancing to the CONCACAF Championship semifinals and, most importantly, qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. That's all to say Saturday's game was meaningful, even if it was less than thrilling. The Americans led 7-0 at halftime and cruised to victory without any semblance of drama. Ashley Sanchez's hat trick was in the bag before halftime, and the Americans' victory was never in doubt. The USWNT recorded 15 shots on goal to El Salvador's zero and dominated possession at a 72-percent clip. There was no statistical category capable of making the rout seem even marginally close. Now that the USWNT has qualified for next summer's World Cup, here's what comes next in the immediate future as the team advances in continental competition. In addition to Sanchez's hat trick, Mallory Swanson, Tierna Davidson and Sophia Wilson also notched goals for the Americans. MORE: Looking ahead to the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups USWNT advance to CONCACAF W Championship semifinals The U.S. will take the field next on Tuesday, Dec. 1, against Jamaica, with kickoff set for 8:30 p.m. ET. Jamaica advanced to the semifinals by virtue of a 3-0 win over Costa Rica and will look to stay hot and score an upset against a heavily favored USA squad. The USWNT has won three straight CONCACAF W Championship titles and has only failed to win the competition twice, in 1998 and 2010, when Canada won both times. When does the 2027 Women's World Cup begin? The 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup will take place in Brazil starting on June 24, 2027 and running for almost exactly a month. The final will be on July 25 in Rio de Janeiro at the famous Maracana Stadium. The draw for the World Cup will be held on December 11 at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio, solidifying the entire group stage with the exception of the three intercontinental playoff qualifiers.

item.description: LAS VEGAS — The Wolverines were without two rotation players in their third and final game of the Players Era 16 tournament at T-Mobile Arena. Starting guard Roddy Gayle Jr. and reserve forward Oscar Goodman were both sidelined and watched Michigan’s 98-69 win over Kansas State from the bench on Friday, Nov. 27. Gayle had his left foot in a boot a day after he was hurt in the Nov. 26 loss against Miami (Fla.) . The injury occurred in the second half when Gayle appeared to roll his left ankle on a drive to the rim. He needed assistance from trainer Chris Williams to get off the court and was on crutches afterward. “He's got a sprained ankle. We held him out today because he really couldn't put pressure on it,” coach Mike Boynton Jr. said. “We don't have our resources to the full capacity here in the hotel. When we get back (to Ann Arbor), we’ll do some more X-rays, make sure there's nothing further there. “But at this point, we think he's going to be fine. We think it'll be a short-term deal. We'll get a better evaluation when we get back to Ann Arbor.” Ricky Liburd replaced Gayle in the lineup and made his first start. For Gayle, who’s averaging 11.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 26.1 minutes, it marked the first game he’s missed this season and third game overall in his three years at Michigan. Goodman, who’s averaging 3.5 points and three rebounds, missed his second straight game with what Boynton described as a “minor” issue. According to a program spokesperson, a medical issue occurred with Goodman shortly after the Nov. 24 loss to Creighton . “Just another evaluation when we get back to Ann Arbor, kind of check his status,” Boynton said. The two combined for 21 of Michigan 32 bench points and turned in their best outings yet. Noland tied his season high with 11 points and dished out seven of Michigan’s 27 assists. Hartman, who made his debut against Creighton after recovering from a preseason shoulder injury, tallied 10 points on 4-for-5 shooting, three assists and two steals in just his third collegiate game. “We think both of those guys can really help us long-term,” Boynton said. “Kenny, we were very intentional about bringing him into our program once we lost L.J. (Cason), having a guy who can be a pretty high floor backup point guard for us. “Joe unfortunately dealt with an injury in the last month or so that's kept him out. item.title: Maple Leafs Announce Multi-Year Contract for Defenseman
item.description: TORONTO, ONTARIO - MAY 4: John Chayka speaks at a press conference where he was announced as General Manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Mats Sundin was introduced as Senior Executive Advisor of Hockey Operations at Real Sports Bar & Grill on May 4, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Michael Chisholm/Getty Images) Getty John Chayka Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs have managed to win two straight games following what was a truly miserable nine-game losing skid that sank them to the bottom of the Atlantic Division standings. The Maple Leafs, who lost defenseman Chris Tanev during Friday’s 3-1 win over the divisional rival Boston Bruins, have announced that they’ve signed 2026 second-round pick Alexander Bilecki, who is currently playing with the OHL’s Kitchener Rangers, to an entry-level contract. The Toronto Maple Leafs Have Signed 2026 Draft Pick Alexander Bilecki To An Entry-Level COntract Getty John Chayka On Friday, the Maple Leafs announced that they had signed 2026 Draft selection Alexander Bilecki to an entry-level contract. “We’ve signed defenceman Alexander Bilecki to a three-year entry-level contract,” the Maple Leafs reported on X, formerly known as Twitter. Soon afterwards, Maple Leafs fans began expressing their approval with the move. “Great to reward his OHL play this season with the contract now,” one fan said. “Great news. Kid looks great this season,” another fan wrote. Another fan said, “WELL YEAH. Would be horrifically dumb if you didn’t.” This fan wrote , “What a snipe by Chayka in the late second round.” Finally, this fan said , “Well deserved. Been a helluva player to start the year in the O.” So far this season with the Kitchener Rangers, Bilecki has scored five goals while adding 23 assists, along with a plus-16 rating. “Just more mature and playing in every situation, power play, penalty kill, overtime, four on four, whatever it may be, being the guy that is relied upon,” Bilecki explained about his playing style via The Toronto Sun . “I’m going out there to help the team win. If I have to lay a hit, block a shot, make a play in the O-zone or score a goal … being able to do it all and being an X factor on the back end for us (is important).” The Maple Leafs Lost Chris Tanev During Friday’s Win The Maple Leafs, despite picking up their second straight win, lost defenseman Chris Tanev, who missed all but 11 games with injuries last season. “Didn’t finish. Never a good sign for me. I don’t have an update. When a guy’s night’s over, it’s never great,” said head coach Jim Hiller. “I just feel really bad for him. He’s obviously missed quite a bit of hockey over the last couple of years. He loves to play, and you just feel bad for him when he’s not able to be out there,” Hiller said. item.description: Jasprit Bumrah overlooked for MI captaincy, reportedly rejects Rohit Sharma's deputy role: Is his future with MI in doubt? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians have officially handed the captaincy back to Rohit Sharma after three disappointing IPL seasons and a dressing room that had lost trust. Jasprit Bumrah was not considered for the top job and reportedly turned down the vice-captaincy offered to him in the first week of October. Bumrah turns 32 in December, and talk is growing that he could explore his options at the 2028 mega auction. MORE: Fans go wild as Rohit Sharma returns as MI captain Will Jasprit Bumrah leave Mumbai Indians after being overlooked for captaincy in IPL 2027? Jasprit Bumrah has been overlooked for the Mumbai Indians captaincy, and the fast bowler has reportedly said no to the chance of serving as Rohit Sharma's deputy, which has raised fresh doubts about whether his long-term future lies with the franchise. Rohit's return to the top job is now official, ending a period of uncertainty that had hung over the five-time champions for some time. The franchise made the move mainly because of its poor results across the last three IPL seasons. A bigger factor, though, was the broken trust inside the dressing room after Hardik Pandya took over as captain. The decision was in fact taken in the first week of October, well before Hardik's move to Punjab Kings was confirmed, which suggests the management had already made up its mind on the way forward, as reported by India Today . Mumbai Indians did not turn to Suryakumar Yadav, even though he led India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year. Bumrah and Tilak Varma, who is currently India's T20 vice-captain, were not seriously looked at either. MORE: Rohit back as MI captain: Inside story of how MI convinced 'Hitman' to take over The franchise has its own reasons for leaving Suryakumar out, and those haven't been made public. Tilak, on the other hand, is still seen as a player who needs more time to develop into a leader. That leaves the question of Bumrah, who is among the most valuable members of the squad. Mumbai Indians don't name a regular vice-captain, but they do need a senior figure to step in when the skipper is unavailable. Suryakumar and Bumrah shared those duties last season while Hardik was out. The franchise did approach Bumrah, but with an offer of the vice-captaincy rather than the top job, since Rohit had already been picked as captain. The offer came from the top leadership in the first week of October. Bumrah politely turned it down, and he alone knows his reasons. His own earlier words add some context. The decision was in fact taken in the first week of October, well before Hardik's move to Punjab Kings was confirmed, which suggests the management had already made up its mind on the way forward, as reported by India Today . Mumbai Indians did not turn to Suryakumar Yadav, even though he led India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year. Bumrah and Tilak Varma, who is currently India's T20 vice-captain, were not seriously looked at either. MORE: Rohit back as MI captain: Inside story of how MI convinced 'Hitman' to take over The franchise has its own reasons for leaving Suryakumar out, and those haven't been made public. Tilak, on the other hand, is still seen as a player who needs more time to develop into a leader. That leaves the question of Bumrah, who is among the most valuable members of the squad. Mumbai Indians don't name a regular vice-captain, but they do need a senior figure to step in when the skipper is unavailable. Suryakumar and Bumrah shared those duties last season while Hardik was out. The franchise did approach Bumrah, but with an offer of the vice-captaincy rather than the top job, since Rohit had already been picked as captain. The offer came from the top leadership in the first week of October. Bumrah politely turned it down, and he alone knows his reasons. His own earlier words add some context. When he was given the stand-in captain's job for the 2026 season, he spoke about how unexpected it all felt. "I didn't think that I will be a Test captain before becoming the MI captain." MORE: ‘There is a deeper issue here’: R Ashwin warns Rohit Sharma's return won't solve Mumbai Indians' problems BCCI/Creimas What next for Bumrah ahead of the 2028 IPL mega auction? Rohit is well known for his man-management, and there is a strong chance he will lead the side for at least two more years, possibly longer. Bumrah will turn 32 early in December, so this may well have been his best and perhaps last real shot at captaining the team. With the top hierarchy looking past him for the leadership group, it remains to be seen whether the moody fast bowler will weigh his choices when the next mega auction takes place before the 2028 season. MORE: Khawaja admits speaking earlier would have ended career; Smith told him to 'shut up' Mumbai Indians may have misread Bumrah Mumbai Indians have been sensible in bringing Rohit back, since the team needed calm and a leader the players trust. Where the franchise may have slipped is in how it handled Bumrah, who has given them more than a decade of service and still isn't being offered the real prize. A vice-captaincy offer to a bowler who has already led the side must have felt, to him at least, like a polite way of saying he wasn't in the long-term plans. His refusal is easy to understand. A player of his stature, who took a pay-cut-free retention deal at Rs 18 crore and kept delivering, would want to be seen as a leader and not as a backup. Fast bowlers also have a short shelf life, and at 32 he can't wait around for a role that may never come. That said, walking away would be a big call. Mumbai is where he became Bumrah, and no other franchise will offer the same comfort and history. The sensible path is an open conversation between the player and the management well before the 2028 auction, because losing him to a rival would hurt far more than any captaincy row. If the talks fail, Mumbai Indians will have only themselves to blame. Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. item.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
item.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as there is of County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season. An assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentinos Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. item.content:encoded: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career.
